title: Fractions: Equivalent Fractions, Comparing, Adding and Subtracting
seo_title: Equivalent Fractions, Comparing, Adding and Subtracting Class 5 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 2)
standard_text: Fractions: equivalent fractions, comparing and ordering fractions, mixed numbers, and adding and subtracting fractions with the same or related denominators (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 5)
meta_desc: Class 5 Fractions worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 2): equivalent fractions, comparing, mixed numbers, adding and subtracting. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply top and bottom by the same number.
key_sub: Make the denominators the same to add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 2/3 = 4/6 = 8/12: equivalent fractions.
  • To compare, use the same denominator: 3/4 = 9/12 > 8/12 = 2/3.
  • 1/4 + 3/8 = 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8.

Examples

Example

Add 1/2 + 1/6.

1/2 = 3/6

3/6 + 1/6 = 4/6

Answer: 2/3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding denominatorsOnly the numerators are added once denominators match.
Comparing only numeratorsMake the denominators equal first.

faq.q: How do you make an equivalent fraction?
faq.a: Multiply or divide the numerator and denominator by the same number.
A whole number and a fraction, like 2 1/4.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
12 = ?8
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts, so each half of the top bar is split into 4 parts. 1 half becomes 1 × 4 = 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
34 = ?8
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 3 quarters become 3 × 2 = 6 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
25 = ?10
items.e: The bottom bar has 10 equal parts, so each fifth of the top bar is split into 2 parts. 2 fifths become 2 × 2 = 4 tenths. So 25 = 410.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
23 = ?12
items.e: The bottom bar has 12 equal parts, so each third of the top bar is split into 4 parts. 2 thirds become 2 × 4 = 8 twelfths. So 23 = 812.

items.q:
The bars are the same size and show the same amount.
34 = ?12
items.e: The bottom bar has 12 equal parts, so each quarter of the top bar is split into 3 parts. 3 quarters become 3 × 3 = 9 twelfths. So 34 = 912.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 12 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 12?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each half is the same as 4 eighths, so 1 half lines up with 1 × 4 = 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many twelfths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each third is the same as 4 twelfths, so 2 thirds line up with 2 × 4 = 8 twelfths. So 23 = 812.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 35 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 35?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each fifth is the same as 2 tenths, so 3 fifths line up with 3 × 2 = 6 tenths. So 35 = 610.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 34 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 34?
items.e: Look down the fraction wall. Each quarter is the same as 2 eighths, so 3 quarters line up with 3 × 2 = 6 eighths. So 34 = 68.

items.q: 56 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 6 × 2 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 2 too: 5 × 2 = 10. So 56 = 1012.

items.q: 23 = ?12
items.e: Look at the denominators: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812.

items.q: 35 = ?20
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 4 = 20. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 = 1220.

items.q: 58 = ?24
items.e: Look at the denominators: 8 × 3 = 24. Multiply the numerator by 3 too: 5 × 3 = 15. So 58 = 1524.

items.q: 47 = ?28
items.e: Look at the denominators: 7 × 4 = 28. Multiply the numerator by 4 too: 4 × 4 = 16. So 47 = 1628.

items.q: 56 = ?30
items.e: Look at the denominators: 6 × 5 = 30. Multiply the numerator by 5 too: 5 × 5 = 25. So 56 = 2530.

items.q: 710 = ?100
items.e: Look at the denominators: 10 × 10 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 10 too: 7 × 10 = 70. So 710 = 70100.

items.q: 14 = ?100
items.e: Look at the denominators: 4 × 25 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 25 too: 1 × 25 = 25. So 14 = 25100.

items.q: 25 = ?100
items.e: Look at the denominators: 5 × 20 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 20 too: 2 × 20 = 40. So 25 = 40100.

items.q: 34 = 15?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 3 × 5 = 15. Multiply the denominator by 5 too: 4 × 5 = 20. So 34 = 1520.

items.q: 25 = 8?
items.e: Look at the numerators: 2 × 4 = 8. Multiply the denominator by 4 too: 5 × 4 = 20. So 25 = 820.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 114 are shaded. Write this as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 3 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So 114 = 2 34.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. 83 are shaded. Write this as a mixed number.
items.e: Each bar is 1 whole. 2 bars are full and 2 more parts are shaded in the last bar. So 83 = 2 23.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. The arrow is 2 marks after 1. So it shows 1 23 = 53.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. The arrow is 1 mark after 2. So it shows 2 14 = 94.

items.q: Write 72 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 2s go into 7? 3 × 2 = 6, so there are 3 wholes. 7 − 6 = 1 is left over. So 72 = 3 12.

items.q: Write 135 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 5s go into 13? 2 × 5 = 10, so there are 2 wholes. 13 − 10 = 3 are left over. So 135 = 2 35.

items.q: Write 174 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 4s go into 17? 4 × 4 = 16, so there are 4 wholes. 17 − 16 = 1 is left over. So 174 = 4 14.

items.q: Write 196 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 6s go into 19? 3 × 6 = 18, so there are 3 wholes. 19 − 18 = 1 is left over. So 196 = 3 16.

items.q: Write 2310 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 10s go into 23? 2 × 10 = 20, so there are 2 wholes. 23 − 20 = 3 are left over. So 2310 = 2 310.

items.q: Write 298 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 8s go into 29? 3 × 8 = 24, so there are 3 wholes. 29 − 24 = 5 are left over. So 298 = 3 58.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 135?
items.e: Each whole is split into 5 equal parts, so each mark is 15. 135 = 2 35: go to 2, then 3 more marks. That is letter C.

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 3 equal parts, so each mark is 13. The arrow is 2 marks after 2. So it shows 2 23 (= 83).

items.q: What number does the arrow show? Give a mixed number.
items.e: Each whole is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. The arrow is 5 marks after 1. So it shows 1 56 (= 116).

items.q: Write 227 as a mixed number.
items.e: How many 7s go into 22? 3 × 7 = 21, so there are 3 wholes. 22 − 21 = 1 is left over. So 227 = 3 17.

items.q: Write 2 35 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 55, so 2 wholes are 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add the 3: 10 + 3 = 13. So 2 35 = 135.

items.q: Write 3 14 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 44, so 3 wholes are 3 × 4 = 12 quarters. Add the 1: 12 + 1 = 13. So 3 14 = 134.

items.q: Write 4 23 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 33, so 4 wholes are 4 × 3 = 12 thirds. Add the 2: 12 + 2 = 14. So 4 23 = 143.

items.q: Write 1 710 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 1010, so 1 whole is 1 × 10 = 10 tenths. Add the 7: 10 + 7 = 17. So 1 710 = 1710.

items.q: Write 5 38 as an improper fraction.
items.e: Each whole is 88, so 5 wholes are 5 × 8 = 40 eighths. Add the 3: 40 + 3 = 43. So 5 38 = 438.

items.q: Which is greater: 58 or 38?
items.e: The denominators are the same, so compare the numerators: 5 > 3. So 58 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 47 or 67?
items.e: The denominators are the same, so compare the numerators: 6 > 4. So 67 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 712 or 912?
items.e: The denominators are the same, so compare the numerators: 9 > 7. So 912 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 16 or 13?
items.e: The numerators are the same. Thirds are bigger parts than sixths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So 13 is greater. The bigger denominator does not make the bigger fraction.

items.q: Which is greater: 110 or 15?
items.e: The numerators are the same. Fifths are bigger parts than tenths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So 15 is greater. The bigger denominator does not make the bigger fraction.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 310?
items.e: The numerators are the same. Fifths are bigger parts than tenths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So 35 is greater. The bigger denominator does not make the bigger fraction.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 58 or 34?
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use eighths: 58 and 34 = 68. 6 > 5, so 34 is greater.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is greater: 23 or 712?
items.e: 12 is a multiple of 3, so use twelfths: 23 = 812 and 712. 8 > 7, so 23 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 710?
items.e: 10 is a multiple of 5, so use tenths: 35 = 610 and 710. 7 > 6, so 710 is greater.

items.q: Which is greater: 49 or 13?
items.e: 9 is a multiple of 3, so use ninths: 49 and 13 = 39. 4 > 3, so 49 is greater.

items.q: Which fraction is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all in sixteenths: 34 = 1216, 58 = 1016, 1116, 12 = 816. The greatest is 1216, so the answer is 34.

items.q: Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: Write them all in twelfths: 23 = 812, 56 = 1012, 712, 512. The smallest is 512, so the answer is 512.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them all in eighths: 1 34 = 148, 158, 1 12 = 128, 138. The greatest is 158, so the answer is 158.

items.e: Write them all in eighths: 34 = 68, 58, 12 = 48. So the order is 12, 58, 34.

items.q:
Order from largest to smallest:
2 13, 136, 2 56
c: 2 56, 2 13, 136
2 13, 136, 2 56
136, 2 56, 2 13
136, 2 13, 2 56
items.e: Write them all in sixths: 2 13 = 146, 136, 2 56 = 176. So the order is 2 56, 2 13, 136.

items.q: Which letter shows 74?
items.e: Each whole is split into 4 equal parts, so each mark is 14. 74 = 1 34: go to 1, then 3 more marks. That is letter D.

items.q: The bar is split into sevenths. Green shows 27 and yellow shows 37. What is 27 + 37?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. The denominator stays 7. The answer is 57.

items.q: The bar is split into fifths. Green shows 15 and yellow shows 35. What is 15 + 35?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 1 + 3 = 4. The denominator stays 5. The answer is 45.

items.q: The bar is split into sevenths. The shaded part is 57, and 37 is crossed out. What is 57 − 37?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Subtract the numerators: 5 − 3 = 2. The denominator stays 7. The answer is 27.

items.q: 15 + 15 + 25 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4. The denominator stays 5. The answer is 45.

items.q: 311 + 511 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 3 + 5 = 8. The denominator stays 11. The answer is 811.

items.q: 29 + 59 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 2 + 5 = 7. The denominator stays 9. The answer is 79.

items.q: 27 + 47 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 2 + 4 = 6. The denominator stays 7. The answer is 67.

items.q: 411 + 611 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 4 + 6 = 10. The denominator stays 11. The answer is 1011.

items.q: 19 + 79 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 1 + 7 = 8. The denominator stays 9. The answer is 89.

items.q: 37 + 17 = ?
items.e: The denominators are the same. Add the numerators: 3 + 1 = 4. The denominator stays 7. The answer is 47.

items.q: The bar is split into quarters. Green shows 12 and yellow shows 14. What is 12 + 14?
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 24. Add the numerators: 24 + 14 = 34. The answer is 34.

items.q: The bar is split into tenths. Green shows 25 and yellow shows 310. What is 25 + 310?
items.e: 10 is a multiple of 5, so use 10 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 25 = 410. Add the numerators: 410 + 310 = 710. The answer is 710.

items.q: The bar is split into eighths. The shaded part is 34, and 18 is crossed out. What is 34 − 18?
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 34 = 68. Subtract the numerators: 68 − 18 = 58. The answer is 58.

items.q:
The bar is split into sixths. The shaded part is 56, and 13 is crossed out. What is 56 − 13?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 3, so use 6 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 26. Subtract the numerators: 56 − 26 = 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 36 by 3 to get 12. The answer is 12.

items.q: The green part is 14 and the yellow part is 38. The dashed lines split the green bar into eighths. How many eighths is the green part?
items.e: Each quarter is split into 2. So 14 = 28: there are 28 in the green part. Now both fractions are in eighths, so you can add or subtract them.

items.q: The green part is 23 and the yellow part is 16. The dashed lines split the green bar into sixths. How many sixths is the green part?
items.e: Each third is split into 2. So 23 = 46: there are 46 in the green part. Now both fractions are in sixths, so you can add or subtract them.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 35?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the numerator by 2 too: 3 × 2 = 6. 35 = 610.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 56?
items.e: 6 × 2 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 2 too: 5 × 2 = 10. 56 = 1012.

items.q: 14 + 38 = ?
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 14 = 28. Add the numerators: 28 + 38 = 58. The answer is 58.

items.q: 13 + 49 = ?
items.e: 9 is a multiple of 3, so use 9 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 39. Add the numerators: 39 + 49 = 79. The answer is 79.

items.q:
A bottle holds 710 L of juice. Ayaan drinks 15 L. How much juice is left in the bottle?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 10 is a multiple of 5, so use 10 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 15 = 210. Subtract the numerators: 710 − 210 = 510. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 510 by 5 to get 12. The answer is 12 L.

items.q:
Rahul walks 34 km to his friend’s house, then 58 km to the park. How far does he walk altogether?
Give your answer as a mixed number.
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 34 = 68. Add the numerators: 68 + 58 = 118. 118 is an improper fraction: 118 = 1 38. The answer is 1 38 km.

items.q:
In a school garden bed, 13 is planted with lettuce and 16 with carrots. What fraction of the garden bed is planted?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 3, so use 6 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 26. Add the numerators: 26 + 16 = 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 36 by 3 to get 12. The answer is 12.

items.q: In a garden bed, 25 is tomatoes and 310 is beans. The rest is herbs. What fraction of the garden bed is herbs?
items.e: First add the parts you know. Use tenths: 25 = 410, so 410 + 310 = 710. The whole garden bed is 1010. Herbs: 1010 − 710 = 310.

items.q: Om has 2 12 m of ribbon. He uses 34 m to wrap a birthday present. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 24. 24 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 2 24 = 1 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. The whole number left is 1. The answer is 1 34 m.

items.q: Rohan and Ishaan share a pizza. Rohan eats 38 of it and Ishaan eats 14. What fraction of the pizza do they eat altogether?
items.e: 8 is a multiple of 4, so use 8 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 14 = 28. Add the numerators: 38 + 28 = 58. The answer is 58.

items.q:
Rehan eats 16 of a pavlova and Varun eats 13 of it. What fraction of the pavlova is left?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: First add what they eat. Use sixths: 13 = 26, so 16 + 26 = 36. The whole pavlova is 66. Left: 66 − 36 = 36. Simplify: 36 = 12.

items.q: Karan runs 1 310 km on Monday and 1 45 km on Tuesday to train for the cross-country. How far does he run in total?
items.e: 10 is a multiple of 5, so use 10 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 45 = 810. Add the fractions: 310 + 810 = 1110. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. 1110 is an improper fraction: 1110 = 1 110. 2 + 1 110 = 3 110. The answer is 3 110 km.

items.q: At the beach, Vivaan swims 45 km. Nikhil swims 710 km. How much further does Vivaan swim than Nikhil?
items.e: “How much further” means subtract. 10 is a multiple of 5, so use 10 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 45 = 810. Subtract the numerators: 810 − 710 = 110. The answer is 110 km.

items.q: A tin holds 2 L of paint. A painter uses 58 L on a fence. How much paint is left in the tin?
items.e: Rename 1 whole as 88: 2 = 1 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 58 = 38. The whole number left is 1. The answer is 1 38 L.

items.q: Neha eats 38 of a pizza. Dev eats 12 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Use eighths: 12 = 48. 4 eighths is more than 3 eighths, so Dev eats more.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Varun eats 34 of it. How many slices does he eat?
items.e: 4 × 2 = 8, so 34 = 68. Varun eats 6 slices.

items.q: At the athletics carnival, Ishaan runs 2 34 km and Tara runs 2 58 km. Who runs further?
items.e: Both ran 2 whole kilometres, so compare 34 and 58. 34 = 68, which is more than 58. So Ishaan runs further.

items.q: Priya says 25 of her class and 410 of her class are the same number of students. Is she right?
c: Yes. 25 = 410
No. 410 is more
You can’t tell without the class size
No. 25 is more
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 25 by 2: 25 = 410. They are equivalent fractions, so they are the same number of students. Yes, she is right.

items.q: For a sausage sizzle, each packet holds 6 sausages. The class cooks 19 sausages. How many packets is that, as a mixed number?
items.e: 6 sausages make 1 packet. 3 × 6 = 18, and 19 − 18 = 1 sausage is left. So 196 = 3 16 packets.

items.q: Four students measure their ribbons. Karan: 34 m. Shreya: 78 m. Varun: 58 m. Gauri: 12 m. Who has the longest ribbon?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68, 78, 58, 12 = 48. The longest is Shreya’s ribbon.

items.q: Nikhil says, “18 is greater than 14, because 8 is greater than 4.” Is he right?
c: Yes. Eighths are bigger than quarters
No. 18 is less than 14
items.e: A bigger denominator means the whole is cut into more, smaller parts. 14 = 28, which is more than 18. So 18 is less than 14.

items.q: Gauri says 2 35 = 65. What is the correct improper fraction?
items.e: Gauri multiplied 2 × 3. Instead, 2 wholes = 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add 3 fifths: 10 + 3 = 13. So 2 35 = 135.

items.q: At sport, Aditya drinks 710 L of water and Isha drinks 35 L. Who drinks more?
items.e: Use tenths: 35 = 610. 7 tenths is more than 6 tenths, so Aditya drinks more.

items.q: In the long jump, Nisha jumps 2 34 m, Rehan jumps 2 58 m and Meera jumps 2 12 m. Order them from the longest jump to the shortest.
items.e: All jumped 2 whole metres, so compare the fractions in eighths: 34 = 68, 58, 12 = 48. So the order is Nisha, Rehan, Meera.
